caption: The Puget Sound Marine Station's laboratory building at Friday Harbor, as published in 1915 (photo courtesy of T. C. Frye): a large gabled frame building on pilings above calm water, a small boat moored below, forest behind.
alt: Sepia photo of a two-and-a-half-storey wooden building with gabled roof and porch, raised on pilings over still water, reflected below, with tall conifers behind.
credit: T. C. Frye, in Nature and Science on the Pacific Coast (American Association for the Advancement of Science, Pacific Coast Committee, 1915); Freshwater and Marine Image Bank, University of Washington Libraries; Public domain

caption: An undated John N. Cobb photograph labeled 'Old lab' on the back: the station's large white waterfront building with a wharf, and tents and a house on the wooded hillside at Friday Harbor.
alt: Black-and-white view across still water to a large white multistory building with a small wharf, tents and a house on the forested slope above.
credit: John N. Cobb, John N. Cobb Photographs, University of Washington Libraries (via Wikimedia Commons); Public domain

caption: The Puget Sound Marine Station on San Juan Island as shown in Wm. E. Ritter's March 1915 Popular Science Monthly article on Pacific coast laboratories: a large white waterfront building, with cottages and tents on the wooded slope behind.
alt: Black-and-white view across water to a wooded shore: a large white building at the waterline, small tents and a house on the slope above.
credit: Unknown photographer, in Wm. E. Ritter, 'The biological laboratories of the Pacific coast', Popular Science Monthly v. 86 (March 1915), via Wikimedia Commons; Public domain

caption: Title page of the first volume of Puget Sound Marine Station Publications, covering 1915-1917, issued under the station's 1909-1917 name before it became the Puget Sound Biological Station.
alt: Plain cream title page with centred capitals reading Puget Sound Marine Station Publications, and Volume 1, 1915-1917 near the bottom.
credit: Puget Sound Marine Station, University of Washington; MBLWHOI Library copy via Internet Archive (Biodiversity Heritage Library collection); licence not stated in the record (Internet Archive metadata: not in copyright)

caption: A 1917 plate from the Puget Sound Marine Station's own publication series: photographs of Desmarestia seaweed specimens illustrating Pease's paper on the genus's taxonomy (page 393, Plate 83).
alt: Printed book page headed '1917 Pease; on Taxonomy of Desmarestia', showing five numbered photographs of branching, leafy seaweed specimens, labelled Plate 83.
credit: Pease, Puget Sound Marine Station Publications (Puget Sound Marine Station, University of Washington, 1917); scan from Biodiversity Heritage Library via Wikimedia Commons; CC0

caption: The Friday Harbor Packing Company cannery on the Friday Harbor waterfront, as published in 1914: a long two-storey plant with its name painted on the wall, boats moored alongside and houses on the hill above.
alt: Black-and-white photo of a long white cannery building at the water's edge, several motorboats moored in front, wooded hillside with houses behind.
credit: Unknown photographer, Pacific Fisherman Year Book 1914, p. 65; Freshwater and Marine Image Bank, University of Washington Libraries; Public domain

caption: Title page of Publications Puget Sound Biological Station, volume 2 (1918-1920), the first volume of the series to carry the name adopted in 1918, after volume 1 appeared as Puget Sound Marine Station Publications.
alt: Plain cream title page with centred capitals reading Publications Puget Sound Biological Station, and Volume 2, 1918-1920 near the bottom.
credit: Puget Sound Biological Station, University of Washington; MBLWHOI Library copy via Internet Archive (Biodiversity Heritage Library collection); licence not stated in the record (Internet Archive metadata: not in copyright)

caption: Contents page of Publications Puget Sound Biological Station, volume 3, nos. 57-58 (May 1921), listing an E. B. Powers paper on marine fish behavior and a J. M. Holzinger and T. C. Frye paper on Alaskan mosses.
alt: Printed journal page headed Publications Puget Sound Biological Station of the University of Washington, with a short contents list and volume details at the bottom.
credit: Puget Sound Biological Station, University of Washington (editors T. C. Frye and T. C. D. Kincaid); Digital Library of India, IARI Library copy, via Internet Archive; licence not stated in the record

caption: The San Juan Canning Company salmon cannery at Friday Harbor, as published in 1914: a long white plant with a tall smokestack on a pile wharf, boats tied up at right and houses on the hill behind.
alt: Black-and-white photo of a long white cannery on a wooden pile wharf over water, a smokestack rising behind, small boats moored to the right.
credit: Unknown photographer, Pacific Fisherman Year Book 1914, p. 65 is IMG009; this image: Pacific Fisherman Year Book 1914, p. 90; Freshwater and Marine Image Bank, University of Washington Libraries; Public domain

caption: Students crowd the launch Jestina and its float at Friday Harbor in July 1922 as the boat takes classes out from the Puget Sound Biological Station. Photograph by John N. Cobb.
alt: Black-and-white photo of a wooden motor launch packed with people, some on its cabin roof, moored beside a crowded float on calm water.
credit: John N. Cobb, John N. Cobb Photographs, University of Washington Libraries (via Wikimedia Commons); Public domain

caption: Three students from the Puget Sound Biological Station's ecology class eat a meal on driftwood logs on a Friday Harbor beach in 1922, photographed by John N. Cobb.
alt: Black-and-white photo of three people, two women in hats and a man, eating from plates while seated on large driftwood logs on a beach.
credit: John N. Cobb, John N. Cobb Photographs (COBB 340), University of Washington Libraries; Public domain

caption: The Puget Sound Biological Station's float and laboratories about 1926, photographed by John N. Cobb: rowboats in the foreground, a ramp up the beach, and two low buildings among tall conifers.
alt: Black-and-white photo of moored rowboats, a wooden walkway up a beach, and two single-story buildings, one with a row of large windows, under tall trees.
credit: John N. Cobb, John N. Cobb Photographs, University of Washington Libraries (via Wikimedia Commons); Public domain

caption: The launch Justine, used by the Puget Sound Biological Station, floats in a rocky cove at Friday Harbor in 1922, one person on deck and a rowboat nearby. Photographed by John N. Cobb.
alt: Black-and-white photo of a wooden motor launch with a small cabin, mast and flag, floating in a calm rocky cove beside a rowboat.
credit: John N. Cobb, John N. Cobb Photographs, University of Washington Libraries (via Wikimedia Commons); Public domain

caption: Plate 2 of Ida Shepard Oldroyd's Marine Shells of Puget Sound and Vicinity (1924), issued as volume 4 of the Puget Sound Biological Station's publications: photographs of Pecten jordani valves and a Lyonsia pugetensis shell.
alt: Page headed 'Oldroyd; on Shells' showing three numbered shells on black: two ribbed scallop valves and an oval shell, labelled Plate 2.
credit: Ida Shepard Oldroyd, Marine Shells of Puget Sound and Vicinity, Publications of the Puget Sound Biological Station v.4 (University of Washington Press, 1924); Freshwater and Marine Image Bank, University of Washington Libraries; Public domain

caption: Cover of Publications Puget Sound Biological Station, volume 4, August 1925: J. W. Hotson's Preliminary List of the Uredinales of Washington (rust fungi), with a round seal and library stamps.
alt: Printed cover with series title, volume and date at top, the title Preliminary List of the Uredinales of Washington, a round seal, and library stamps.
credit: J. W. Hotson; Puget Sound Biological Station, University of Washington; CABI Library Archive copy via Internet Archive; licence not stated in the record

caption: A montage of embryos, larvae and adult marine invertebrates, mixing micrographs and color photos, showing organisms studied in Friday Harbor Laboratories' Comparative Invertebrate Embryology course in 2006.
alt: Collage of colorful marine invertebrates and gray microscope images of larvae and embryos, including curled orange animals, a small jellyfish and early cell clusters.
credit: Bruno Vellutini, via Flickr and Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 2.0

caption: Julian Voss-Andreae's stainless-steel sculpture 'Steel Jellyfish' (2006), whose file title links it to green fluorescent protein (GFP), stands among boulders on a lawn at Friday Harbor Laboratories; photographed March 2007.
alt: A tall open lattice of angular stainless-steel bars, like a twisted ribbon, standing on grass between lichen-spotted boulders, with trees and a wooden building behind.
credit: Julian Voss-Andreae (photographer and sculptor), via Wikimedia Commons (transferred from English Wikipedia); CC BY-SA 3.0

caption: Friday Harbor Laboratories' docks under a pink sky in June 2021: a red-hulled boat with a crane and smaller craft moored beside a wooden dock building, a snow-capped peak on the horizon.
alt: Calm water at twilight: a red-hulled boat with a crane and smaller boats at a wooden dock, forested shore and a distant snowy mountain.
credit: Chiwauk (own work), via Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 4.0

caption: A broad August 2015 view of Friday Harbor Laboratories from a Washington State Ferry: the long two-story waterfront building at left, docks with small boats in the middle, and lower buildings among the forest.
alt: Forested shoreline with a long two-story building at left, a floating dock and small boats at center, and smaller buildings among tall evergreens.
credit: Joe Mabel, via Flickr and Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 3.0

caption: Friday Harbor Laboratories from a Washington State Ferry, August 2015: a long two-story building with many windows stands at the shoreline above a floating dock, with other station buildings and forest beyond.
alt: Waterfront view of a long two-story building with rows of windows and a dark hipped roof, a dock with small boats, and conifer forest behind.
credit: Joe Mabel, via Flickr and Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 3.0
